product.title: Cap Crash
product.summary: Rebuild a roster after the cap crashes, then defend the plan to a boardroom.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students sign, cut and trade under a reduced cap while four meters move, hit a single trade-deadline pressure moment forcing a win-now or stay-flexible call, lock a strategy, then write a boardroom memo defending it before receiving a front-office grade.

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Pure logic separated from UI with two passing test suites and a README explaining the design rationale — the strongest engineering of any single-lesson repo. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. No defects found and no dominant strategy: buying the highest-talent players affordable produced four players, 37 wins and an illegal roster, while buying value produced thirteen players, 41 wins and chemistry 95. Depth beating star-stacking is a real, non-obvious result, and the roster-size rule closes the obvious exploit. Season variance is separate from the choices and labelled as such.

curation.tierBasis: A genuinely open sandbox with a non-obvious result: buying the best affordable players produced four players and 37 wins, buying value produced thirteen and 41. The roster-size rule closes the star-stacking exploit by construction, and season variance is separated from the choices.
